turns: Under the Payment of Wages Act 1936, by what date must my employer pay my monthly wages?

case_file.summary: User asks under the Payment of Wages Act 1936 by what date the employer must pay monthly wages.

replies.text:
**Where you stand**  
For employees paid on a monthly basis, the employer must pay the wages **before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month** [1][2].

**What you can do**  
1. Send a written demand to your employer asking for payment by that deadline.  
2. If the employer does not pay, you may issue a legal notice stating the statutory deadline and that you will file a claim.  
3. File a wage claim with the authority appointed under the Code on Wages (usually a labour officer) - the claim must be made within **three years** from when the wages became due [3][5].

**Next step**  
Draft and send a written demand to your employer, specifying that the wages are overdue and must be paid **by the seventh day of the next month** as required by law. Keep any proof of employment (offer letter, payslips, bank statements) you have, as it will be needed if you later file a claim. If you receive no response within a reasonable time (e.g., 7-10 days), consider issuing a legal notice or filing a claim.

If you like, I can draft a legal notice for you to send - just say "draft the notice".

*LawBuddy gives legal information, not legal advice.*

passages.header: Code on Wages, 2019, section 17 (text) | salary | statute
passages.title: Code on Wages, 2019, section 17 (text)
passages.text:
**17. Time limit for payment of wages.** (1) The employer shall pay or cause to be paid wages to the employees,
engaged on,
(i) daily basis, at the end of the shift;
(ii) weekly basis, on the last working day of the week, that is to say, before the weekly holiday;
(iii) fortnightly basis, before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight;
(iv) monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.
(2) Where an employee has been, (i) removed or dismissed from service; or (ii) retrenched or has resigned from
service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two
working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), the appropriate Government may,
provide any other time limit for payment of wages where it considers reasonable having regard to the circumstances
under which the wages are to be paid.
(4) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall affect any time limit for payment of wages provided
in any other law for the time being in force.

passages.header: Unpaid salary or final dues: your rights | salary | guide
passages.title: Unpaid salary or final dues: your rights
passages.text:
Wages are governed by the Code on Wages, 2019, which replaced the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act,
1948, the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 (Code on Wages, 2019, s. 69).

"Employee" under the Code covers anyone employed on wages by an establishment to do skilled, semi-skilled, unskilled,
manual, operational, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work, except apprentices and
members of the Armed Forces (Code on Wages, 2019, s. 2(k)).

**When wages must be paid** (Code on Wages, 2019, s. 17(1)):
- daily workers: at the end of the shift;
- weekly: on the last working day of the week;
- fortnightly: before the end of the second day after the fortnight ends;
- **monthly: before the seventh day of the next month ends.**

**When you leave.** If you resign, or are removed, dismissed or retrenched, or the establishment closes, the wages due
to you must be paid **within two working days** (Code on Wages, 2019, s. 17(2)).

The government may set other time limits in some circumstances (s. 17(3)). Karnataka's own rules under the Code were
still in draft when LawBuddy's sources were collected, so check with the Karnataka Labour Department for procedure.

passages.header: Steps to recover unpaid salary | salary | guide
passages.title: Steps to recover unpaid salary
passages.text:
1. **Written demand** to HR or the owner by email, listing the unpaid months and amounts and a date to pay by.
2. **Legal notice** if there is no payment: facts, amounts, the legal deadline for payment, and a warning that you
   will file a claim. LawBuddy can draft one for you to review and sign.
3. **Wage claim** before the authority appointed under the Code on Wages (ask the Karnataka Labour Department which
   officer hears claims for your area), within three years (Code on Wages, 2019, s. 45(6)). This is usually faster and cheaper than court, and can award compensation
   of up to ten times the claim (s. 45(2)).
4. **Civil suit** as an alternative: a suit for wages must be filed within three years from when the wages became
   due (Limitation Act, 1963, Schedule, Article 7). Talk to a lawyer or the DLSA before choosing this route.

Free help: industrial workmen are among those entitled to free legal services (see "Free legal aid").

passages.header: Laws that have been replaced | general | guide
passages.title: Laws that have been replaced
passages.text:
Many websites and older documents still quote laws that have been repealed. Do not rely on them:

- The **Consumer Protection Act, 1986** was repealed by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (s. 107). Consumer
  complaints now go to District, State and National Consumer **Commissions** (earlier called Forums).
- The **Payment of Wages Act, 1936**, the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**, the **Payment of Bonus Act, 1965** and the
  **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976** were repealed by the Code on Wages, 2019 (s. 69).
- The **Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961** was replaced by the Karnataka Rent Act, 1999 (s. 70).
- The **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** and the **Indian Evidence Act** were
  replaced in 2024 by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya
  Adhiniyam. Criminal matters are outside LawBuddy's scope; see a lawyer.

passages.header: Code on Wages, 2019, section 45 (text, extract) | salary | statute
passages.title: Code on Wages, 2019, section 45 (text, extract)
passages.text:
**45. Claims under Code and procedure thereof.** (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or
more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and determine the claims which arises under the
provisions of this Code.
(2) The authority appointed under sub-section (1), while deciding the claim under that sub-section, may order,
having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensation in addition to the claim
determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined and endeavour shall be made by the authority to
decide the claim within a period of three months.
(3) If an employer fails to pay the claim determined and compensation ordered to be paid under sub-section (2), the
authority shall issue a certificate of recovery to the Collector or District Magistrate of the district where the
establishment is located who shall recover the same as arrears of land revenue and remit the same to the authority
for payment to the concerned employee.
(4) Any application before the authority for claim referred to in sub-section (1) may be filed by, (a) the employee
concerned; or (b) any Trade Union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 of which the employee is a member; or
(c) the Inspector-cum-Facilitator.
(6) The application under sub-section (4) may be filed within a period of three years from the date on which claims
referred to in sub-section (1) arises: Provided that the authority referred to in sub-section (1) may, entertain the
application after three years on sufficient cause being shown by the applicant for such delay.
